nodes.statement: It is possible to write a program that outputs an exact copy of its own source code.
nodes.span: write a source program that, when compiled and executed, will produce as output an exact copy of its source.

nodes.statement: A self-reproducing program can include additional, unrelated code that is also reproduced.
nodes.span: contain an arbitrary amount of excess baggage that will be reproduced along with the main algorithm.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the general capability of a program to reproduce its own source code

nodes.statement: A compiler can be trained to recognize new constructs by temporarily using lower-level equivalents to bootstrap the new binary.
nodes.span: We must "train" the compiler. After it "knows" what "\v" means, then our new change will become legal C.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the step-by-step explanation of bootstrapping the compiler with a decimal value

nodes.statement: A compiler can be modified to intentionally miscompile specific source code patterns.
nodes.span: deliberately miscompile source whenever a particular pattern is matched.
nodes.status_reason: the reader model understands compilers and can accept they can be modified to alter output

nodes.statement: A compiler bug could alter the login command to accept a backdoor password.
nodes.span: miscompile the login command so that it would accept either the intended encrypted password or a particular known password.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the general concept of a compiler bug applied to a specific target

nodes.statement: Malicious code placed directly in the compiler's source code would be easily noticed by reviewers.
nodes.span: Even the most casual perusal of the source of the C compiler would raise suspicions.
nodes.status_reason: relies on the reader's general understanding that malicious code is visible in source

nodes.statement: A self-reproducing program can be used as a Trojan horse to automatically inject malicious code into future compilations.
nodes.span: The replacement code is a Stage I self-reproducing program that inserts both Trojan horses into the compiler.
nodes.status_reason: combines the concepts of a self-reproducing program, excess baggage, and a compiler bug

nodes.statement: Once the infected compiler binary is installed, the malicious code can be removed from the source, leaving no visible trace while still infecting future compilations.
nodes.span: remove the bugs from the source of the compiler and the new binary will reinsert the bugs whenever it is compiled.
nodes.status_reason: follows from bootstrapping the compiler trojan so the binary retains the bug after source removal

nodes.statement: Examining the source code is insufficient to guarantee that a program is free of malicious behavior.
nodes.span: No amount of source-level verification or scrutiny will protect you from using untrusted code.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the fact that the bug exists only in the binary and leaves no trace in the source

nodes.statement: You cannot fully trust any software unless you wrote all of it, including the tools used to build it.
nodes.span: You can't trust code that you did not totally create yourself.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the failure of source-level verification

nodes.statement: This type of self-propagating attack can be implemented in any software that processes other programs, such as assemblers or microcode.
nodes.span: I could have picked on any program-handling program such as an assembler, a loader, or even hardware microcode.
nodes.status_reason: the reader model cannot derive this for microcode but can verify the author's assertion

nodes.statement: Malicious bugs become increasingly difficult to discover when they are placed in lower-level system components.
nodes.span: As the level of program gets lower, these bugs will be harder and harder to detect.
nodes.status_reason: follows from the fact that lower level tools compile the higher level ones

nodes.statement: Unauthorized access to computer systems is a serious offense akin to burglary, not a harmless prank.
